_comment: Every Type.property the served surface cannot write, SPLIT BY INTENT. `hole` = nothing can set it and somebody would want to. `machine_written` = an operation writes it and a caller parameter would be wrong, so `written_by` names that operation. `unused` = nothing writes it and nobody has carried it. A flat count conflated the first two and could not be read as a to-do list. `vocabulary_reach.py --check` fails when a NEW unreachable property appears that this file does not classify. | 2026-09-20: the cross-type pool was removed from vocabulary_reach.py, so a property is judged against the tools that write ITS type. Eight entries were added in that pass, and Requirement.kind and Verification.location left this list by gaining real parameters.

entries.reason: 0 of 295 carry one. THE CORE TAKES NO CLOCK by design, so a creation timestamp can only ever be caller-supplied, and no caller has wanted one.
entries.written_by: (the core never reads the system time)

entries.reason: reconcile_artifacts records when the file was last OBSERVED to match. A caller-set value would assert an observation nobody made.
0 of 295. A function signature or part number; declared, never wanted.

1 of 108 carries one, written through the generic escape hatch, and no typed tool accepts it. The schema calls it 'where it lives — a source dir, a physical location, a document path', which is the direct analogue of Artifact.location, and add_component does not take it. Recorded as a hole rather than given a parameter because one instance in 108 is not yet evidence that anyone wants it; the count is the thing to watch.
0 of 8. A constraint's reason is carried by its statement and by the decision that imposed it; the bare property has never been written.
register_alternative writes the options considered. Hand-setting the JSON would let a caller claim a fork nobody registered.
2 of 202, both through create_node. Same no-clock reason.
entries.written_by: (the core never reads the system time)

entries.reason: 40 of 40. drift.rs composes it as '<artifact_id> drift' when it records the event. A caller-set name would let two drifts on one artifact read as unrelated, and the event is not something a caller creates by hand.
Set when the drift is dispositioned, by the accept that resolved it.
Computed by the pass that found the drift.
The finding's own message, written by the reconcile pass that detected the drift. A caller-set summary would describe a drift nobody observed.
0 of 221. Same no-clock reason.
entries.written_by: (the core never reads the system time)

Written by mirror_surface with what the mirror actually brought in.
Written by mirror_surface; it names the design mirrored FROM.
The date the mirror was taken, written by the act of taking it.

57 of 57 carry one, all written by the same gap_to_prompt path that writes `question` — but no setter appears in the source for it, so it is recorded as unwritten-by-the-surface pending a look at how it lands.
